video_title: The Knicks Are Feeling Their Overbooked Offseason | Rachel Nichols & Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers' defensive success and offensive struggles early in the season
quotes.excerpt: They are top five in the NBA defensively, that's good. They're bottom five in the NBA offensively.
quotes.quote: They are top five in the NBA defensively, that's good. They're bottom five in the NBA offensively, that's bad, but they've been able to win some pretty good games to start the season, including the opening night win against the Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers' concerns regarding three-point shooting and rebounding
quotes.excerpt: They're bottom third in the league in three-point makes and that was projected to be an issue.
quotes.quote: They're bottom third in the league in three-point makes and that was projected to be an issue for this team coming into the season. LeBron James, basically an inside the three-point line guy now. Jaylen Brown, an inside the three-point line guy now. Joel Embiid can't shoot threes, but you don't want him shooting threes, you want him exploiting mismatches in the post or making mid-range jumpers at the high post. They're not a great three-point shooting team and will that cost them if they can't get into the middle of the pack, close to the top 10 in three-point percentage? And rebounding, that's a problem for this group.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers' rebounding issues following Joel Embiid's injury
quotes.excerpt: They lost Ariel Hukporti for the season with that Achilles tear. Adem Bona is okay.
quotes.quote: They lost Ariel Hukporti for the season with that Achilles tear. Adem Bona is okay, but when Joel Embiid is off the floor, they've got real problems when it comes to rebounding the basketball. So if they don't get better contributions from their backup bigs, that's something that could rear its head as problematic, especially as they go up against these big teams that are out there.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Thunder's potential to trade Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.excerpt: Would the Thunder make Isaiah Hartenstein available, given that Ousmane Dieng looks like he's ready to play?
quotes.quote: Would the Thunder make Isaiah Hartenstein available, given that Ousmane Dieng looks like he's ready to play? Because Ousmane Dieng is ready to play. The guy is legit. And if you're looking around saying, Isaiah Hartenstein is available, don't you think New York is going to pick him up? I think they would try really hard, but I think the Thunder could ask for a king's ransom for Hartenstein at that point because I think there would be a bidding war for a player like that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum's role in the Jaylen Brown trade
quotes.excerpt: I believe that Jaylen Brown believes that not that Jayson Tatum asked for him to be traded.
quotes.quote: I believe that Jaylen Brown believes that not that Jayson Tatum asked for him to be traded, but that Jayson Tatum could have stopped it. That's what I believe. Not reporting that, that's just kind of my read of the tea leaves that's out there. That Jayson Tatum, as the face of the franchise, if he wanted to stop this deal from going down, he could have, and he didn't do it. And that's why he's saying cap on all that with Tatum.
